question: A shipment of dried figs originating from Türkiye is found to contain aflatoxin B1. Which EU legislation is relevant to this case?

plan.question: Identify the EU contaminant legislation in the frozen corpus relevant to aflatoxin B1 in dried figs, and retrieve the provisions and annex entries needed to assess the product category and any use- or processing-dependent distinctions.
plan.search_query: EU contaminant maximum levels aflatoxin B1 dried figs Regulation 2023/915 product category intended use sorting physical treatment annex legal text
plan.expected_evidence_type: Retrieved regulation text and applicable annex entries, with evidence IDs; distinguish the regulation’s own annex from any amending act’s annex

plan.question: Determine whether EU legislation in the frozen corpus provides special import controls for dried figs originating in Türkiye, and identify the product, hazard, and origin conditions that govern applicability.
plan.search_query: Regulation (EU) 2019/1793 Türkiye dried figs aflatoxins increased official controls annex product origin conditions
plan.expected_evidence_type: Retrieved import-control regulation text and relevant annex entries, with evidence IDs; applicability conditions rather than assumptions about this consignment

plan.question: Identify the general EU food-law provisions in the frozen corpus relevant to food-business-operator responsibilities for food placed on the market when a contaminant is detected.
plan.search_query: Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 unsafe food food business operator responsibility traceability withdrawal notification relevant provisions
plan.expected_evidence_type: Retrieved operative legal text with evidence IDs on operator responsibilities and conditional duties

plan.question: Identify the EU official-controls legislation in the frozen corpus relevant to controls on imported food and competent-authority actions, including any interaction with special import-control rules.
plan.search_query: Regulation (EU) 2017/625 imported food official controls competent authority measures non-compliance relevant provisions interaction Regulation 2019/1793
plan.expected_evidence_type: Retrieved official-controls legal text with evidence IDs; distinguish general rules from any product-specific import requirements

evidence.location: Article 19 — Responsibilities for food: food business operators
evidence.text: Article 19 Responsibilities for food: food business operators 1. If a food business operator considers or has reason to believe that a food which it has imported, produced, processed, manufactured or distributed is not in compliance with the food safety requirements, it shall immediately initiate procedures to withdraw the food in question from the market where the food has left the immediate control of that initial food business operator and inform the competent authorities thereof. Where the product may have reached the consumer, the operator shall effectively and accurately inform the consumers of the reason for its withdrawal, and if necessary, recall from consumers products already supplied to them when other measures are not sufficient to achieve a high level of health protection. 2. A food business operator responsible for retail or distribution activities which do not affect the packaging, labelling, safety or integrity of the food shall, within the limits of its respective activities, initiate procedures to withdraw from the market products not in compliance with the food-safety requirements and shall participate in contributing to the safety of the food by passing on relevant information necessary to trace a food, cooperating in the action taken by producers, processors, manufacturers and/or the competent authorities. 3. A food business operator shall immediately inform the competent authorities if it considers or has reason to believe that a food which it has placed on the market may be injurious to human health. Operators shall inform the competent authorities of the action taken to prevent risks to the final consumer and shall not prevent or discourage any person from cooperating, in accordance with national law and legal practice, with the competent

Article 1 Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply: (a) ‘food’ means food as defined in Article 2 of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 1 ); (b) ‘food business operator’ means food business operator as defined in Article 3, point 3, of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002; (c) ‘placing on the market’ means placing on the market as defined in Article 3, point 8, of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002; (d) ‘final consumer’ means final consumer as defined in Article 3, point 18, of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002; (e) ‘processing’ means processing as defined in Article 2(1), point (m) of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 2 ); (f) ‘unprocessed products’ means unprocessed products as defined in Article 2(1), point (n), of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004; and (g) ‘processed products’ means processed products as defined in Article 2(1), point (o), of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004.

Food business operators shall collaborate with the competent authorities on action taken to avoid or reduce risks posed by a food which they supply or have supplied.

Article 18 Traceability 1. The traceability of food, feed, food-producing animals, and any other substance intended to be, or expected to be, incorporated into a food or feed shall be established at all stages of production, processing and distribution. 2. Food and feed business operators shall be able to identify any person from whom they have been supplied with a food, a feed, a food-producing animal, or any substance intended to be, or expected to be, incorporated into a food or feed. To this end, such operators shall have in place systems and procedures which allow for this information to be made available to the competent authorities on demand. 3. Food and feed business operators shall have in place systems and procedures to identify the other businesses to which their products have been supplied. This information shall be made available to the competent authorities on demand. 4. Food or feed which is placed on the market or is likely to be placed on the market in the Community shall be adequately labelled or identified to facilitate its traceability, through relevant documentation or information in accordance with the relevant requirements of more specific provisions. 5. Provisions for the purpose of applying the requirements of this Article in respect of specific sectors may be adopted in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 58(2).

evidence.location: Article 19 — Specific rules on official controls and for action taken by the competent authorities in relation to the residues of relevant substances in food and feed
evidence.text: Article 19 Specific rules on official controls and for action taken by the competent authorities in relation to the residues of relevant substances in food and feed 1. Official controls to verify compliance with the rules referred to in points (a) and (c) of Article 1(2) shall include official controls, to be performed at any stage of production, processing and distribution, on relevant substances including substances to be used in food contact materials, contaminants, non-authorised, prohibited and undesirable substances whose use or presence on crops or animals or to produce or process food or feed may result in residues of those substances in food or feed. 2. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 144 to supplement this Regulation by laying down rules for the performance of the official controls referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article and for action to be taken by the competent authorities following those official controls. Those delegated acts shall lay down rules on: (a) specific requirements for the performance of official controls, including, where appropriate, the range of samples and the stage of production, processing and distribution where the samples are to be taken in compliance with the methods to be used for sampling and laboratory analyses established in accordance with points (a) and (b) of Article 34(6), having regard to the specific hazards and risks related to substances referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article; (b) the cases where the competent authorities in relation to non-compliance or suspicion thereof are to take one or more of the measures referred to in Articles 137(2) and 138(2); (c) the cases where the competent authorities in relation to non-compliance or suspicion thereof of animals and goods

The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, lay down rules on uniform practical arrangements for the performance of the official controls referred to in paragraph 1 and for action to be taken by the competent authorities following those official controls, regarding: (a) uniform minimum frequency of such official controls, having regard to the hazards and risks related to substances referred to in paragraph 1; (b) specific additional arrangements and specific additional content to those provided for in Article 110, for the preparation of the relevant parts of the multi-annual national control plan (MANCP) provided for in Article 109(1); (c) specific practical arrangements for the activation of the mechanism of administrative assistance provided for in Articles 102 to 108. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 145(2). 4. For the purpose of Article 30, the delegation of certain official control tasks, referred to in this Article, to one or more natural persons shall be allowed.

Article 17 Responsibilities 1. Food and feed business operators at all stages of production, processing and distribution within the businesses under their control shall ensure that foods or feeds satisfy the requirements of food law which are relevant to their activities and shall verify that such requirements are met. 2. Member States shall enforce food law, and monitor and verify that the relevant requirements of food law are fulfilled by food and feed business operators at all stages of production, processing and distribution. For that purpose, they shall maintain a system of official controls and other activities as appropriate to the circumstances, including public communication on food and feed safety and risk, food and feed safety surveillance and other monitoring activities covering all stages of production, processing and distribution. Member States shall also lay down the rules on measures and penalties applicable to infringements of food and feed law. The measures and penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

## 1. Short answer

The relevant legislation identified by the supplied evidence is:

- **Regulation (EU) 2023/915** — for contaminant maximum levels. Its supplied table lists dried figs at **6.0 μg/kg for aflatoxin B1** and **10.0 μg/kg for the sum of aflatoxins**. Detection alone does not establish an exceedance. [E84bba6f619]
- **Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1793** — for special import controls. A supplied Annex II snapshot lists Türkiye-origin dried figs and specified fig products for aflatoxins and ochratoxin A, with a **30% frequency of identity and physical checks**. The snapshot does not establish that the listing currently applies to this consignment. [E4eb1cdcb42] [Effd100d7a6]
- **Regulation (EU) 2017/625** — the general official-controls framework; the supplied Article 19 text covers controls on contaminants at production, processing and distribution stages. [Ef624e98067]
- **Regulation (EC) No 178/2002** — food-business-operator responsibilities, including conditional withdrawal and notification duties where the stated conditions are met. Detection alone does not establish that those duties are triggered. [E32d56f6d3a] [E46c1b89564]
- **Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2782** — relevant to sampling and analysis for mycotoxins, including aflatoxins, where the consignment is covered by the applicable 2019/1793 listing and conditions. [E6755b594ef]

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

The supplied 2023/915 table says the dried-fig limits also apply to food consisting only of dried figs and to processed products consisting of at least 80% dried figs; other cases refer to Article 3(1) and (2). The product’s composition, intended use, measured B1 concentration and applicable sampling/analysis basis are not provided. [E84bba6f619]

The 2019/1793 snapshot lists dried figs under CN code **0804 20 90**, alongside other specified fig products. That code is a listing, not confirmation of this shipment’s actual classification. [Effd100d7a6]

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

**Practical next checks:** obtain the measured concentration and sampling/analysis results; confirm the product composition and intended use; verify the shipment’s CN/TARIC classification and product scope; and check the current official 2019/1793 Annex entry and applicable conditions. Do not treat the 30% figure as a current shipment-specific requirement without that verification.

**Critical uncovered investigation issues:**
- **Legal evidence:** the specific imported-food control and competent-authority action rules, and their interaction with the special import listing, are not established by the supplied evidence.
- **Current law:** the current legal effect of the 2019/1793 Annex II listing and check frequency is unverified.
- **Case facts:** the consignment’s actual classification and whether its product falls within the listing are not established.
- **Case facts / legal applicability:** the measured aflatoxin B1 result and the applicable 2023/915 product-category conditions are not established.
